text:
emily_support: FYI escalated from Acme — invoice 2026-03-12 shows ~18.2k more billed tokens than served tokens in dashboard. Customer is worried. https://app.redwood.com/invoices/INV-7861 :eyes:

olga_support: Ack, can you paste sample request IDs or traces? :eyes:

emily_support: Here's the last 3 traces they attached:
```
trace_id=tx-9a8b7c req_id=R-axa123 path=/v1/complete model=redwood-1 size=4096 served_tokens=34 metered_tokens=246
trace_id=tx-9a8b7d req_id=R-axa124 path=/v1/complete model=redwood-1 size=1024 served_tokens=0 metered_tokens=512 prefetch=true
trace_id=tx-9a8b7e req_id=R-axa125 path=/v1/embeddings model=embed-1 size=128 served_tokens=0 metered_tokens=128 prefetch=true
```

emily_support: They say served tokens (what returned) don't match invoice metering.

tariq_billing: Looking. At first glance metered_tokens > served when prefetch/warmup triggered by c-batcher/prefetch. Could be warmup prefetch counted. :thinking:

chen_runtime: Did they use continuous batcher (ctbatch) or explicit prefetch? Logs show `prefetch=true` in some traces. The runtime currently bills prefetch token generation when the kernel executes, not at final send time.

olga_support: Is that by design? Should prefetch be charged if result later served from KV prefix cache?

chen_runtime: Today we charge when the inference is executed (kernel run) — prefetch warms KV cache and does decode work. But there's an edge: if a later request hits prefix/KV cache and short-circuits, we still previously paid for the prefetch. So invoice shows metered work > served.

tariq_billing: Customer expectation is billed==served or at least clear docs. We need to figure repro, magnitude, and whether it's a bug or doc/UX gap.

emily_support: Repro steps I tested in staging:
```
# 1) send warmup prefetch via background client
POST /v1/prefetch {"prefix": "The quick brown" }
# 2) then send many tiny requests that hit prefix
POST /v1/complete {"prompt": "The quick brown fox" }
```
I see metered increments on the prefetch run, served tokens on the subsequent hits are small.

chen_runtime: That matches. Can you capture `runtime.trace` for both runs with `--detailed-metering` enabled? It will show `meter_event` entries.

emily_support: Captured and attached. snippet:
```
[meter] event=kernel_exec tokens=2048 type=prefetch trace=tx-9a8b7c
[meter] event=prefetch_cache_hit tokens=0 trace=tx-9a8b7d
```

olga_support: Next steps?

tariq_billing: 1) patch billing docs to explain prefetch counts. 2) short-term: enable per-customer opt-out for prefetch billing (support toggle). 3) long-term: change attribution so metering attributes token cost to first customer-visible served request, or mark warmup prefetch as billable only if its output used.

chen_runtime: Implementation note: attributing costs to later request is tricky with concurrent batcher and dedup. We'll need a lightweight attribution token that survives cache hit and amortizes cost across consumers. I can spin up an RFC.

emily_support: Customer wants immediate relief. Can we refund the 18.2k tokens and disable prefetch for their account?

tariq_billing: I'll open invoice adjustment ticket and flag for temporary credit. Also toggle `account.prefetch_billing=false` for Acme.

billing-bot: action_taken=credit_created amount=18,200_tokens ticket=INV-7861

emily_support: Thanks. Proposed follow-ups:
- chen to write RFC on attribution (due EOW)
- tariq to confirm credit applied and update docs
- olga to send customer status update

chen_runtime: RFC started: https://go/repo/rfcs/kv-prefetch-metering

olga_support: I'll send update now. :rocket:

emily_support: Closing loop here, will re-open if more gaps.
